title: Assessment of Creativity Potential of a 3DGAN in Implant Crown Design
content: Digital dentistry increasingly relies on artificial intelligence to automate restorative design. Yet the ability of generative networks to produce multiple clinically plausible solutions for the same prosthetic field remains insufficiently evaluated. This study assessed the creative potential of a previously developed three-dimensional generative adversarial network (3DGAN) for screw-retained implant crown design. Nine AI-generated implant crown designs were analyzed, consisting of three independently generated crowns for each of three different prosthetic fields. Within each set, the crowns were superimposed and compared using “MeshLab”. Mean HD, maximum HD, and RMS values were recorded, with 0.05 model units used as the threshold for identifying insufficient morphological variation. The overall mean HD was 3.32 model units, the mean maximum HD was 16.18 model units, and the mean RMS value was 4.40 model units. No pairwise comparison showed values equal to or below 0.05 model units. In conclusion we found that the investigated 3DGAN demonstrates real creative potential.
